steps.text: Gather the ingredients. Preheat the oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
Spread 1 can of chili and beans in the bottom of a 9x13-inch baking dish.
Roll up franks inside tortillas and place in baking dish, seam side down, on top of chili and bean layer. Top with remaining can of chili and beans, and sprinkle with cheese.
Cover baking dish with aluminum foil, and bake in the preheated oven for 30 minutes. Enjoy!

raw_recipe.headline: Chili Dog Casserole
raw_recipe.description: This chili dog casserole has layers of beef franks, chili with beans, tortillas, and Cheddar cheese for a simple and delicious casserole.

video.description: The recipe in this video is wonderful for outdoor cookouts, and it can be made ahead. It is loved by young and old alike! There is no better way to use up an extra pack of hot dogs and a few cans of chili.
video.name: How to Make Chili Dog Casserole

review.reviewBody: Where has this recipe been all my life??? Absolutely wonderful! I used fat free doggies, added onion, cheese, and mustard inside the fat-free tortilla and used homemade chili instead of canned. My, my, my....what wonderful comfort food! Thank you Maxine!

I REALLY enjoy preparing and serving this dish. First time I made it was around 2003. I’ve won two summertime potluck contests with it! My family and friends all have nothing but the best compliments when I make it. I’ve been vegetarian since 2011, so use veggie hot dogs and still vegetarian and carnivores both come for seconds. This is a recipe I will always enjoy serving, no matter the season. It’s right up there with my Tater Tot Casserole, but even better! I especially appreciate how easy it is to make and how delicious it is, plus leftovers are so good! Ps. I dress the hot dog with ketchup and mustard inside the tortillas. Then top the finished product with sour cream just before serving for a little extra deliciousness!
Used cheddar filled dogs and added onion. Only other recommendation is to cook uncovered! Crispy crunchy cheese is the best!

I've made a similar recipe for several years now, calling it Enchilidog Casserole. I use 2 cans chili with beans, a 10 oz can red or green enchilada sauce, 8 bun-length franks or hot dogs, 8 8-10" tortillas, half a chopped onion and about 8 oz shredded Cheddar (we like sharp). Pour half the can of enchilada sauce in a 9" x 13" dish. Fill each tortilla with a couple spoons-full of chili, a sprinkle of onions and cheese and lay each one in the casserole. Once they're all in, pour over the rest of the enchilada sauce (and chili if there's any left), sprinkle over more cheese. Cover with foil and bake at 375 degrees F for 30 mins. Yummy and thanks for reminding me of this!

I ALWAYS read reviews before cooking, and followed many suggestions, used what I had & my husband’s picky criteria. Made for 4, Hebrew National hot dogs are favorites, and had on hand. Cut hotdogs down middle, added small slices of x sharp cheddar, broiled till cheese was melted. (I maintained regular oven rack place for general baking.) Removed hot dogs from casserole, then greased casserole pan with olive oil. Moved to Cincinnati recently, ‘Skyline Chili’ is all over Cincinnati. Local stores carry their chili canned. I had a can. No beans, good for my husband will eat NO beans! I combined 1/3 quinoa with 2/3 rice. When combination was cooked I added about 2 ounces of Skyline Chili. Put combination on bottom of casserole. Putting hot dogs in tortilla shells –added about a tbsp. chili to each, rolled up, laid in casserole. Set oven at 400. Covered casserole with remaining chili (½ a can) spread on all surfaces, baked 7-10 minutes – removed –sprinkled ¼ cup extra sharp cheddar shredded, back in oven till cheese was melted. My husband did not leave a scintilla of quinoa or rice . . . and he never mentioned anything. Nothing means good. This is added to the ‘husband will eat’ relatively short list!

This fit the bill for some left-over hot dogs and chili I had in the fridge. Following some of the other reviewers suggestions, I put onions, cheese, and some of the chili in the tortilla before wrapping the hot dog in it. I also used small, taco sized tortillas and fried them on each side in butter to keep them from getting soggy (that's how my son likes it whenever I make enchiladas). Then more chili, onions, cheese, and jalapenos on top before baking. Yum!

This was so easy and so family friendly! The only change I made was to remove the foil for the last few minutes of cooking time to crisp up the top slightly. It would also be fun to experiment with different toppings, like chopped red onion and sour cream.

I have made this recipe just as is for years, and everyone loves it. This time, I heated the tortilla over the gas flame, spread some refried beans and sprinkled on some chopped onions, and rolled up the heated hot dogs in the tortilla, spread the chili and cheese, and put in the oven. Garnished with some pickled jalapenos. Why I didn't think of this before?! This year I'm going to do this as an appetizer for Christmas using the little hot dogs, and sizing the tortillas.

First of all I made in a smaller casserole dish which worked out great since it was perfect size for hotdogs. I also used hormel Coney Island chili sauce on top layer, all beef franks and topped with sour cream and franks red hot! Very easy and quick. Highly recommend

Tried for the first time tonight. I LOVE chili dogs and had to try it. My husband isn't wasn't a fan. But I liked it a lot. The fact that there isn't a whole lot of bread with the hot dogs is a plus. Used Ballpark Beef Franks for the weenies and steamed them before wrapping them like others had suggested. Worked out great. The only change I made was not only adding mustard and onions in the wrap, but also added a whole lot more of both to the dogs before the cheese layer. I didn't cover it while it baked. Cheese browned up nicely and made a crunchy layer on top. Added more mustard (what can I say? I'm a condiment lover!) to mine and it was perfect! Don't think I can make this for a family meal again because of my husband. 😔 But I can sure make this for myself anytime I like now that I have the recipe! Thanks for sharing it. 👍

9.3.21 I was sitting out on the porch, and I didn’t hear the timer go off so, unfortunately, I did overcook a bit. Not to worry, this was still surprisingly good! I had chili in the freezer, so I used that instead of canned chili (sorry, wouldn’t go there). Interesting, because in spite of cooking longer than it should have, the hot dog still was just warm, not hot. Next time, I think I’ll cover the dish with foil for 20 minutes, then remove the cover for the last 10 minutes for the cheese to melt. I garnished with TJ’s hot and sweet peppers and served with Mexican Street Vendor Style Corn Salad and Instant Pot® Refried Beans, both recipes from this site. It just doesn’t get much easier than this for a tasty Friday night comfort food meal, and I wouldn’t hesitate to make this again.
Good the way it was might try with onion and mustard next time. Also remove cover last 10 minutes
Didn’t like outcome

I make this with no-bean chili, hotdogs and cheese. It’s one of my favorites. Use a good quality hotdog. I’m going to use chili with beans the next time I make it. The beans will add fiber, always a good thing. I haven’t wrapped the hotdogs in tortillas, but will try that too. Another variation is to use frozen burritos instead of hotdogs, it’s great. I use a 10 ounce can of enchilada sauce for that. I love easy Tex-Mex.
Delicious. Very easy recipe to cut in half, although I still used almost two cans of chili.
You can make it with no beans and also the Johnsonville Brats as well.
I added some mustard and onions
i would just brown the weiners before wrapping them in their tortillas. my husband and toddler enjoyed it! it made about 4 and a half servings, with 9 taco/fajita sized tortillas. (certainly not 10!)
I don't understand all the changes made to the recipe. It is perfect as is!
Taste amazing even picky eaters in my house love it
